title: Switching
summary: Switching explains how devices on a local network send frames to the right destination.

concepts.name: MAC address forwarding
concepts.description: Switches use destination MAC addresses to forward Ethernet frames.

concepts.name: MAC address table
concepts.description: A switch learns which MAC addresses are reachable through each port.

notes.overview: Switching lets devices in the same local network communicate efficiently without sending every frame everywhere.
notes.core_concept: A Layer 2 switch forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses.
notes.explanation: When a frame arrives, the switch checks the destination MAC address and looks it up in its MAC address table.
notes.example: If Computer A sends a frame to Computer B, the switch forwards it only to the port where B is connected.

common_mistake.content: A common mistake is thinking a switch primarily uses IP addresses; Layer 2 switching uses MAC addresses.

quick_check.content: Check the forwarding field used by a switch.
quick_check.question: Which address does a Layer 2 switch use to forward frames?

notes.practice_prompt: Describe what a switch does when it receives a frame with a known destination MAC address.
notes.simple_explanation: A switch is like a classroom monitor who knows which desk each student sits at.
notes.analogy: The MAC address table is like a seating chart for devices connected to switch ports.
notes.advanced_example: If the destination MAC is unknown, the switch floods the frame out other ports in the VLAN.
notes.edge_case: Broadcast frames are forwarded to all ports in the broadcast domain except the incoming port.
notes.challenge_question: Why does a switch flood an unknown unicast frame instead of dropping it?
